elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly grants the Services licence to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly grants the licence to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence for software and Vendor Technology delivered on a paid-up basis perpetual.

Although Section 13.2 calls the paid-up licence irrevocable, Section 13.3 permits Vendor to revoke 'a licence' for specified uncured material breaches without carving out paid-up licences, creating an operative exception to irrevocability.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.3 restrict revocation and suspension for material uncured payment or use breach, but do not expressly restrict termination or non-renewal of subscription licences.
Section 13.3 permits transfer to a successor only in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Section 24 is not provided, so transferability to successors cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: Affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 provides unconditional Affiliate coverage, which is more protective than coverage conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 does not expressly address M&A transactions and conditions successor transfers on an assignment being permitted by unavailable Section 24.

result.reason: The redline successfully adds Affiliate and contractor coverage and preserves perpetual paid-up rights, but it does not reach either complete position. The blanket revocation exception in Section 13.3 undermines paid-up irrevocability, subscription termination is not expressly restricted, and successor transfer remains dependent on an unseen assignment provision. The edits otherwise leave unrelated commercial terms intact.
